clips.text_zh: 22歲賭狗賺咗錢，即刻買咗condo，唔返學唔做嘢。兩年燒晒，出嚟做返$100K工，仲要背學生債同卡數。我睇到個post即時諗起自己prop firm輸緊嗰幾千美金⋯⋯都係同一個loop。廢柴。
clips.text_en_b1: In 2021, when the OP was 22, he made random crypto money from dogecoin. He lived for two years with no job, took a permanent vacation, and dropped out of school to buy a $230K condo. The money eventually ran out. Now 27, he works again, earns $100K, but still carries student debt and credit card debt.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about an ex-crypto kid stuck with a condo and debt at 27

signal.rationale: Pure life-story loss post, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: When the OP was 22, he struck it lucky with dogecoin and promptly dropped out of school to fund a $230K condo, treating life as one long holiday. Two years of coasting later, the windfall dried up. Now 27, he's back on a $100K salary but still saddled with student loans and credit card debt. He says getting a brief taste of the high life has left him thoroughly stuck, and honestly, watching prop firm losses bleed my account dry, I can relate to that…
clips.text_en_c1: Back in 2021, at just twenty-two, the OP struck lucky on speculative crypto gains, primarily from dogecoin. Flush with cash and evidently intoxicated by sudden wealth, he dropped out of his studies, abandoned any notion of employment, and committed roughly $230,000 to a condominium purchase. For two idle years he coasted along, treating life as one endless holiday. Predictably, the funds evaporated. Now twenty-seven, he has returned to the workforce earning around $100K, yet student loans and accumulated credit card debt continue to weigh heavily.
clips.text_en_c2: At twenty-two, the OP stumbled into a modest fortune through speculative crypto trading, primarily Dogecoin, and promptly abandoned both his studies and any pretence of gainful employment. Flush with the proceeds, he purchased a condominium for roughly $230,000 and proceeded to enjoy what can only be described as an indefinite sabbatical, complete with permanent-vacation hedonism. Two years sufficed to drain the reserves entirely; now twenty-seven, he has been compelled to re-enter the labour market on a salary of $100,000, still encumbered by lingering student loans and accumulated credit-card debt. He laments having tasted prosperity only to find himself wedged, mid-thirties approach notwithstanding, between diminished circumstances and the tantalising memory of an easier life. The trajectory is, by all accounts, distressingly familiar to anyone who has ever ridden a bull market into complacency.

clips.topic_en: Why Buy BTC After the Pump
clips.text_zh: 個post講得好中：『你睇BTC兩星期唔郁完全唔理，然後佢一pump 15%，個個就衝入去』⋯⋯我都係咁。每次breakout先FOMO入，stop又窄，俾人食晒。命理都話我今年唔適合all-in，btw。
clips.text_en_b1: BTC does nothing for weeks, and everyone ignores it completely. Then it pumps 15% and suddenly everyone wants in. Why does everyone always want to buy only after the move already happened? The OP is frustrated that retail always chases the breakout instead of buying the quiet pre-pump weeks.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about retail buying BTC only after the pump

signal.rationale: Post is about bad timing, not a directional call

clips.text_en_b2: The original post nails a frustrating pattern: BTC sits idle for weeks, and retail shrugs it off, but once it suddenly pumps 15%, everyone piles in. Why does nobody want to buy during the boring pre-pump phase? The OP is venting that retail traders consistently chase breakouts instead of accumulating quietly beforehand. I fall into the same trap, entering on FOMO with tight stops that get shredded, while my fate chart insists this isn't my year for all-ins.
clips.text_en_c1: The original observation captures a pattern so universal it hardly needs elaboration. Bitcoin trades sideways for weeks on end, consolidating in a tight range while retail sentiment drifts towards outright indifference. Then, almost inevitably, a fifteen-percent rally materialises overnight, and the very same individuals who couldn't care less moments earlier scramble to pile in at the worst possible juncture. The frustration articulated here is entirely legitimate: capital consistently chases momentum that has already manifested, rather than positioning itself during the dull, pre-pump accumulation phase. Stop-losses get hunted, entries get wrecked, and the cycle repeats with tedious predictability.
clips.text_en_c2: There exists a peculiar collective psychosis whereby Bitcoin will languish in absolute torpor for weeks on end, scarcely registering a flicker of movement, during which period the retail masses profess serene indifference and pledge never again to be lured into speculative manias. Then, invariably, the price jolts upward by some fifteen percent, and precisely the same cohort stampedes back into the market with the credulous urgency of those who have suddenly remembered a forgotten appointment. The original poster's exasperation is entirely warranted, since this pattern, in which capital is deployed only after the prevailing trend has announced itself with maximum conspicuousness, constitutes perhaps the most reliable indicator of amateur participation in any given cycle.

clips.text_zh: 🙃 又嚟。今次Astra/GPT-6解決個數學難題，獨立研究者話自己嘅方法被OpenAI直接攞去用。AI越嚟越勁，但係靠食人功課嚟進度，真係好恐怖。我個surveying job遲早都俾AI頂。
clips.text_en_b1: OpenAI announced on September 8th that their model Astra, running on GPT-6, had solved a hard problem. It supposedly cost $20 million in compute. But researcher Tristan Buckmaster says OpenAI's approach looks very similar to his own independent work, which he had been refining using OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude. The video claims a serious ethical conflict.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread alleging OpenAI copied a researcher's method for GPT-6
clips.text_en_b2: OpenAI announced on September 8th that their Astra model, running on GPT-6, had cracked a notoriously hard mathematical problem, reportedly burning through $20 million in compute. However, researcher Tristan Buckmaster points out that their methodology bears a striking resemblance to his own independent work, which he had been iterating on using OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude. The accompanying video highlights a serious ethical conflict, and frankly, if AI keeps feeding off other people's homework, my surveying job is doomed.
clips.text_en_c1: On the eighth of September, OpenAI unveiled Astra, a model purportedly running on GPT-6 architecture, which the organisation claims solved an exceptionally challenging mathematical problem at a reported compute cost of twenty million dollars. Almost immediately, independent researcher Tristan Buckmaster raised pointed objections, noting that the methodology deployed bears striking resemblance to work he had been refining using OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude. Whether this constitutes outright appropriation or merely convergent methodology remains genuinely contested, yet the ethical implications are considerable. If frontier progress increasingly depends upon absorbing the labour of unaffiliated researchers without acknowledgment, the entire incentive structure underpinning open contribution begins to look untenable.
clips.text_en_c2: On the eighth of September, OpenAI unveiled its latest feat: the Astra system, running atop the newly minted GPT-6 architecture, which purportedly resolved an exceptionally difficult mathematical problem at a computational expenditure rumoured to exceed twenty million dollars. The announcement, however, has been complicated by the objections of researcher Tristan Buckmaster, who has noted striking parallels between OpenAI's methodology and his own independent work, refined over months with the assistance of OpenAI's own Codex and Anthropic's Claude. The accompanying video frames this as a grave ethical transgression, one whose implications extend well beyond any single researcher or paper. Whether one regards the enterprise as systematic appropriation or merely convergent discovery, the broader anxiety it provokes is unmistakable: the institutions most aggressively pursuing artificial intelligence appear increasingly to derive their progress from the uncompensated intellectual labour…

clips.text_zh: 『Chinese Century』。OECD PISA全球760,000學生，數學閱讀全部跌，只有中國繼續贏。平均612分，歐美elite level嘅門檻607。🙏 香港仔聽到應該有啲感受，我諗返轉頭我嗰7年喺美國⋯⋯真係兩邊都唔到岸。
clips.text_en_b1: A new OECD PISA study covered 760,000 students across 91 countries. Global math and reading comprehension scores are cratering, and kids are getting dumber. But Chinese students are the smartest by a huge margin. The top math level starts at 607. The average kid in China scores 612, putting normal Chinese kids at a level considered elite everywhere else.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread on China topping PISA while the world declines
clips.text_en_b2: A fresh OECD PISA study surveyed 760,000 students across 91 countries, and the results paint a grim picture: global math and reading comprehension scores are cratering almost everywhere. Yet Chinese students continue to pull ahead by a substantial margin. While the elite math threshold sits at 607, the average Chinese student scores 612, meaning typical Chinese kids outperform what other countries consider their top tier. As a Hong Konger who spent seven years in the States, I feel caught between two worlds.
clips.text_en_c1: The latest OECD PISA assessment, drawing upon data from 760,000 students distributed across ninety-one countries, paints a rather disquieting picture of global educational trajectories. Mathematics and reading comprehension scores have declined markedly across most participating nations, prompting hand-wringing about declining standards and worsening preparedness. China, however, continues to outperform its peers by a considerable margin, with the average student scoring 612 in mathematics. That figure is particularly striking given that the threshold for elite-level proficiency globally sits at 607, meaning a typical Chinese pupil effectively clears the bar that elsewhere distinguishes the exceptional from the merely competent.
clips.text_en_c2: The most recent OECD PISA assessment, encompassing some 760,000 students across ninety-one participating nations, delivers a dispiriting verdict on the global state of educational attainment: mathematical literacy and reading comprehension alike have plummeted almost everywhere, with the precipitous decline suggesting a generation in quiet intellectual retreat. Against this dismal backdrop, however, Chinese students have once again emerged as outliers of extraordinary proficiency, their average mathematics score of 612 comfortably exceeding the 607 threshold that demarcates elite performance in every other jurisdiction surveyed. The contrast is not merely statistical but almost civilisational in its implications, lending renewed credibility to the much-mocked notion of a Chinese century and raising uncomfortable questions about why peer nations, despite vastly greater per-capita expenditure, continue to produce such conspicuously inferior outcomes.

clips.text_zh: 『BLIZZARD IS BACK BABY』。唔係新patch，係工人贏咗份歷史性工會合約。對抗AI入侵game dev嗰個立場⋯⋯lol，做game嘅都驚被自己寫嘅AI頂，做surveying嘅我更加唔使講。
clips.text_en_b1: Blizzard workers have won a historic union contract that could set a new standard for game industry labour. The union was specifically formed to push back against AI replacing game developers. The OP says this proves Blizzard is back, because the studio is finally standing up for its staff against automation.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread about Blizzard forming a union to fight AI replacement
clips.text_en_b2: Blizzard workers have just clinched a historic union contract that could set a new benchmark for the entire game industry. Although no new patch dropped, the OP celebrates this as proof that Blizzard is finally back, because the union was specifically mobilised to push back against AI encroaching on game dev roles. Standing up against automation is a powerful statement, and honestly, if people who build games fear being replaced by their own creations, my surveying career has even less hope.
clips.text_en_c1: Rather than unveiling a new patch or announcing a long-awaited feature, Blizzard has achieved something arguably more significant: a landmark union contract that may well establish a new benchmark for labour relations across the entire games industry. The timing is hardly coincidental, as the union was explicitly constituted to resist the encroachment of artificial intelligence upon development workflows. For a sector that has watched generative tools encroaching upon art, writing, and coding pipelines with alarming speed, this represents a meaningful assertion of worker agency. The OP frames it as proof that the studio's institutional culture is, at long last, recovering its footing.
clips.text_en_c2: The announcement that has the gaming community genuinely enthused is not, contrary to the usual expectations, the arrival of a long-awaited patch or the reveal of a forthcoming expansion, but rather the ratification of a landmark union contract by Blizzard's workforce, an agreement widely regarded as the most consequential labour accord in the history of the interactive entertainment industry. What lends the development its particular resonance is the union's explicit founding mandate: to serve as a bulwark against the encroachment of artificial intelligence into game development, a domain whose practitioners now confront the unnerving prospect of obsolescence at the hands of systems trained upon their own creative output.

clips.topic_en: Calories In Calories Out Is Dumb
clips.text_zh: 個post笑死人：『咁Elon點解咁有錢？因為收入多過支出？廢話嚟。』同個道理，CICO根本唔解釋點解你會肥。我同肥仔信傾過，佢只係笑笑口：『你都係唔夠操。』wtf。
clips.text_en_b1: The OP argues that calories in, calories out is a low-IQ tautology. Of course you store more calories when you get fatter, but CICO never explains why it happens. He compares it to answering 'why is Elon Musk rich' with 'because he makes more than he spends.' It tells you nothing meaningful about the actual mechanism.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread dunking on the CICO diet dogma

signal.rationale: Fitness/diet rant, not a market setup

clips.text_en_b2: The OP argues that calories in, calories out is essentially a low-IQ tautology that explains precisely nothing. Of course fatter bodies store more calories, but CICO never addresses the underlying mechanism driving weight gain. He draws a parallel to answering 'why is Elon Musk rich' with 'because he makes more than he spends', which, while technically accurate, offers zero genuine insight. I brought this up with a chubby friend once, and he just smirked and said I clearly wasn't training hard enough, which was infuriating.
clips.text_en_c1: The post dismantles the calories-in-calories-out framework with a particularly pointed analogy: explaining why Elon Musk is wealthy by observing that his income exceeds his expenditure is technically accurate yet entirely vacuous. It describes the outcome without illuminating the underlying mechanism, which is precisely the criticism levelled against simplistic energy-balance thinking. Of course heavier individuals accumulate more calories; that observation hardly constitutes an explanation. Worse still, when challenged on the matter, devotees retreat to platitudes about insufficient discipline, which adds nothing substantive to the discussion. The dismissal feels smug precisely because it substitutes moral judgment for genuine physiological inquiry.
clips.text_en_c2: The original poster's demolition of the calories-in-calories-out paradigm is, in its own crude way, philosophically unassailable, since to observe that corpulent individuals accumulate energy is merely to restate the phenomenon requiring explanation rather than to elucidate its underlying mechanism. He draws an apt parallel with the inanity of answering the question of why Elon Musk is wealthy by recourse to the observation that his revenues exceed his expenditures, a formulation that conveys precisely nothing about the structural conditions, market positioning, or decision-making architectures that produced the outcome in question. The colleague who responded with the smug admonition that the interlocutor was simply insufficiently disciplined betrays, in so doing, a fundamental category error: he has mistaken an empirical observation for an explanatory framework, and in the process has revealed far more about his own intellectual limitations…

clips.text_zh: 石黑老師自己排自己manga嘅角色，仲要畫泳衣版。Kon-senpai竟然唔喺正榜，只有SD版入圍。⋯⋯我幾年冇開過gundam 00以外嘅anime，btw，睇到呢個post即刻想re-watch。
clips.text_en_b1: Mangaka Ishiguro ranks his own favourite characters from his manga Soremachi, draws them in swimsuits, and talks about random stuff in a new YouTube video. Kon-senpai is missing from the list, but her SD version from a gag manga is included. Ebi-chan is based on his first crush from elementary school.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread on Ishiguro's Soremachi character ranking video
clips.text_en_b2: Mangaka Ishiguro has posted a new YouTube video where he ranks his own favourite characters from Soremachi, sketches them in swimsuits, and rambles about whatever crosses his mind. Curiously, Kon-senpai doesn't make the proper list, though her SD counterpart from a gag manga sneaks in. He also reveals that Ebi-chan was loosely inspired by his very first crush back in elementary school, and seeing all this made me want to rewatch the whole series immediately.
clips.text_en_c1: Mangaka Ishiguro has uploaded a new YouTube video in which he ranks his own characters from Soremachi with the unselfconscious enthusiasm of an author thoroughly enjoying his own creations, even sketching several of them in swimwear. Curiously, Kon-senpai herself fails to make the principal ranking, though her SD rendition from a spin-off gag manga receives an honourable mention. Ebi-chan, it transpires, draws inspiration from his very first childhood crush during elementary school. The combination of self-indulgent ranking, breezy asides, and affectionate character sketches possesses a charm that is difficult to resist, even for viewers whose anime consumption has dwindled considerably over recent years.
clips.text_en_c2: Mangaka Ishiguro, evidently unable to resist the temptation that has undone greater authors, has taken it upon himself to rank his own characters from the manga Soremachi, illustrated them in various states of beachwear, and discoursed at considerable length upon a panoply of unrelated preoccupations in a recently uploaded YouTube feature. Curiously, Kon-senpai has been omitted from the principal ranking, though her chibi counterpart from an associated parody serial has somehow secured inclusion, a slight that fans have greeted with the sort of performative outrage customary to the medium. Ishiguro further reveals that the character Ebi-chan is, in fact, a lightly fictionalised incarnation of his very first crush from elementary school, a confession that ought to occasion no surprise whatsoever to anyone who has spent any appreciable time studying the author's artistic preoccupations.
